alternatives.concept: Study modern Italy through European and Mediterranean history, comparative politics, international relations, national identity, sociology, art, film and cultural research. This is a related humanities and social-science route; it preserves the absence of Italian-language proficiency and a cumulative Italy-specific disciplinary sequence.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines modern European and Mediterranean history, politics, sociology, Renaissance Italy, art-historical research, literature, film and media. alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic, artistic and media forms create cultural meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, Renaissance Italy, film and multimodal production. Preserve Italian-language acquisition, Italian linguistics, translation and sustained Italy-specific depth as explicit gaps.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, Renaissance Italy, film, media and cultural identity; it does not claim Italian proficiency or a full Italian Studies curriculum.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Ten courses / 75 EC differ in each direction. Comparative politics, international relations, modern sociology, EU politics, historical research, peace and conflict, Western military history, documentary study and art-historical research are replaced by literary studies, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, media archaeology, life writing, popular media and community communication. The change shifts the programme from Italy in European and Mediterranean historical-political context to language, literature and mediated cultural identity.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eleven level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term and none has a formal prerequisite. Introductory history, politics, sociology, Mediterranean art history, literature and film precede advanced EU politics, archival research, conflict, social theory, persuasion, literary-film, media and art-historical research. No Italian-language prerequisite or proficiency is implied.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. The first studies Italy through European and Mediterranean history, politics, society, identity, art and cultural research; the second develops literature, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film, media and cultural identity. A third Italian-proficiency and linguistics programme is not feasible because the current workbook contains no Italian acquisition sequence, Italian grammar, sociolinguistics, translation or Italian-language academic writing. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as Italian proficiency.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine language structure, processing and change; UCR provides general psycholinguistics rather than a history of Italian or Italian-language study.
UCR has no Italian-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 1.
UCR has no Italian-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 2.
UCR has no Italian-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 3.
UCR has no Italian-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 4.
UCR has no advanced Italian-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 5.
UCR has no advanced Italian-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 6.
UCR has no Italian-to-Dutch translation course or Italian translation-practice sequence.
Both study Italy within wider regional and cross-cultural relations; UCR concentrates on Renaissance Italy and the global Mediterranean rather than a general regional-studies introduction.
Both study major European literary works in historical and cultural context; UCR is comparative and translation-based rather than part of an Italian-language sequence.
Both analyse film as cultural representation; UCR studies adaptation and film-text relations comparatively rather than concentrating on Italian cinema.
Both situate modern Italy within nationalism, state formation, war and European political and social change; UCR is comparative rather than Italy-specific.
Both examine political authority, national identity, borders and territoriality; UCR provides political philosophy rather than the comparator humanities-philosophy course.
Both examine national identity in a European political setting; UCR focuses on EU institutions, legitimacy and policy rather than a dedicated Italian Studies identity course.
Both introduce humanities and social-science approaches to society and culture; UCR supplies a sociology foundation rather than an integrated humanities survey.
Both analyse contested national identity and public culture; UCR approaches these through contemporary social theory rather than an Italy-specific seminar.
UCR has no cumulative Italian Studies introduction combining Italian language, history, politics and culture.
The compulsory 30-EC Italy Studies semester abroad remains separate and is not replaced by scheduled UCR courses.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
The compulsory Italian Studies thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study modern European and Mediterranean history, Italian Renaissance art, politics, national identity, sociology, literature, film, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and cultural research. UCR does not offer Italian proficiency progression, Italian grammar and sociolinguistics, translation, Italian-language academic work or the compulsory semester in Italy, so these are related humanities and social-science routes rather than Italian Language and Culture equivalents.
